how-much-does-turo-take-from-hosts.html.text:
← Back to the Turo host payout calculator

How much does Turo actually take from hosts?

Not one percentage — a matrix. Turo restructured host earnings around March 2026 into three named earnings plans, and within each plan the host share also depends on how far ahead of the trip the guest booked. The rest of this page works through the matrix on a real trip price, not a rounded example.

The matrix

Host share by earnings plan and booking window (the guest's fraction goes to Turo):

Plan0-2 days ahead3-13 days ahead14-27 days ahead28+ days ahead
Peace of Mind ($250 cap)65%70%75%80%
Balanced ($1,500 cap)75%80%85%90%
More Earnings ($2,750 cap)85%90%95%100%

The percentage applies to the trip price plus any extra-mileage, late-return, and additional-usage fees the guest owes — not just the headline daily rate. The “cap” column is each plan's commonly cited damage-responsibility limit: the dollar amount a host can be held responsible for if the vehicle is damaged on a trip. It does not enter the payout arithmetic, but it is the real trade-off behind picking a higher-share plan.

Worked example

A host lists a $350 trip (1 day, no extra fees) on the Balanced plan, booked 3-13 days ahead.

FigureArithmeticResult
Host shareBalanced × 3-13 days80%
Host payout$350 × 0.80$280.00
Turo's cut$350 − $280.00$70.00 (20%)

The same $350 trip, every plan, same booking window

PlanHost payoutTuro's cutDamage cap
Peace of Mind$245.00$105.00$250
Balanced$280.00$70.00$1,500
More Earnings$315.00$35.00$2,750

A $70.00 swing on one trip from plan choice alone — against a damage-exposure range running from $250 to $2,750 over the same three rows.

The same $350 trip, Balanced plan, every booking window

Booking windowHost shareHost payout
0-2 days ahead75%$262.50
3-13 days ahead80%$280.00
14-27 days ahead85%$297.50
28+ days ahead90%$315.00

A $52.50 swing on the identical trip, from booking timing alone — nothing about the trip itself changed.

What that adds up to over a month

At 6 trips like this one a month, on the Balanced plan at the 3-13-day window: $280.00 × 6 = $1,680.00 a month, or $20,160.00 a year — a linear projection from one trip's payout and a stated trip frequency, not a booked-calendar forecast.

Do this with your own trip

The Turo host payout calculator runs this same arithmetic on your own trip price, plan, booking window, and any extra fees, compares all three plans and all four booking windows side by side, and projects a monthly and annual estimate from your own trip frequency. Nothing you type leaves your browser.

Common questions

How much does Turo actually take from hosts in 2026?

Somewhere between 0% and 35%, depending on two things you pick or the guest picks: your earnings plan (Peace of Mind, Balanced, or More Earnings) and how far ahead of the trip the guest booked (0-2, 3-13, 14-27, or 28+ days). On the Balanced plan, Turo's cut ranges from 25% (last-minute) down to 10% (28+ days out). There is no single "Turo takes X%" answer anymore -- the honest answer is a 12-cell matrix, not a percentage.

Why does the same trip pay differently depending on when it was booked?

Turo's host share locks in at the moment the guest books, and every earnings plan pays more the further ahead that booking happens. A trip booked 28+ days out pays a meaningfully higher host share than the identical trip booked 0-2 days before it starts, under all three plans -- it rewards a host's listing being bookable further in advance, not the trip itself being any different.

Which earnings plan should I pick?

That depends on how much weight you put on host share versus damage-responsibility exposure, which this page cannot decide for you. Peace of Mind pays the lowest share (65-80%) but caps a damage claim you could be held responsible for at a commonly cited $250. More Earnings pays the highest share (85-100%) but raises that cap to a commonly cited $2,750. A higher share is not free money -- it comes with more of your own vehicle's risk on your side of the line.

vs-a-spreadsheet.html.text:
← Turo host payout calculator

This calculator vs. a spreadsheet

A lot of hosts already track payouts in a spreadsheet: one column for trip price, one for the host-share percentage, a formula that multiplies them. That arithmetic is trivial and a spreadsheet does it fine once you already know which host-share percentage to type in. What it does not do on its own is hold Turo's whole plan-by-booking-window matrix -- three earnings plans times four booking windows is twelve possible host-share cells for the same trip, and a plain spreadsheet has no built-in way to check that the cell you used actually matches the plan and window you have.

QuestionWhere to answer it
What's trip price times host share? Either one — a spreadsheet multiplies fine.
Which of the twelve plan x booking-window cells applies to this trip? This calculator — you pick the plan and the window, it derives the share; a spreadsheet needs you to already know the answer before you can build the formula.
What would this exact trip have paid under the other two plans? This calculator — a full plan comparison table, generated automatically from the same trip.
What would this exact trip have paid if the guest had booked earlier or later? This calculator — a full booking-window comparison table, same trip, same plan.
If I mistype the host-share percentage, will anything catch it? This calculator — the share is derived from your plan and window, never typed in directly, so the two can't drift apart.
Is anything I enter uploaded anywhere? No, on either — but this calculator needs no account, no template, and no formula to maintain.
Calculate a Turo payout now

This tool needs no account and nothing installed: it is a static page, the arithmetic runs in your browser, and the trip price, plan, booking window, and every fee you enter stay on this device — nothing is uploaded anywhere.

Common questions

Isn't a Turo payout just trip price times host share?

The multiplication itself is trivial and a spreadsheet does it fine once you already know the right host-share percentage to type in. What a plain spreadsheet does not do on its own is hold Turo's whole plan-by-booking-window matrix — three earnings plans times four booking windows, twelve possible host-share cells for one trip — so you have to already know which cell applies before you can even start the formula.

Why is comparing plans and booking windows harder in a spreadsheet than it looks?

Seeing what the same trip would have paid under a different plan, or if the guest had booked earlier or later, means building and maintaining eleven more formula cells alongside the one you actually need — and updating all twelve every time the trip price or extra fees change. This calculator recomputes the full plan comparison and the full booking-window comparison automatically, from the same inputs, every time you calculate.

What happens if I type a percentage into the wrong cell in my own sheet?

Nothing — a spreadsheet returns whatever the formula says, whether the host-share percentage you typed matches the plan and booking window you actually have or not, and there is no built-in check that the two agree. This calculator derives the host share from the plan and booking window you select, so the two can never disagree, and it flags findings like a missing trip price rather than silently returning zero or a stale number.

Does this replace a host's own income-tracking spreadsheet?

No. A spreadsheet or ledger that tracks every trip, every payout, and every month's total over a year is still the right tool for that ongoing record. This page answers one question at a time — what does this trip pay under my plan and booking window, and what would it have paid under the other eleven combinations — and nothing it computes is saved anywhere once you leave the page.
